chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Smith and Parker's mutual influence
summary: Smith says Parker followed him and he did not copy Parker, and he left New York before Bebop.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: How would you describe the difference between you and Charlie Parker as people?
About the same. It looked like he tried to follow me, and I followed behind him!
Yes, actually that's a point. Were you influenced by him to any extent?
Yeah, I believe so. Because it looked like he would do anything I did...
I mean, were there things that he would play, and you'd think, 'Wow! I never thought of that.'
No. I didn't try to copy behind him. No. Not at all. I never did try to copy from him.

To what extent at the time you and he were working together... Were you ever trying to experiment with harmony and sort of trying to introduce new passing chords into things? Were you, to any extent influenced by what became called Bebop later,
by the idea of running passing chords, those chromatic things on the minor sevenths? Were you doing that?
No. They started that after I left New York.
So this was not something you were into.
Well, I can hear it in your playing sometimes.

Yeah. It might have been. But I never did... They started all that after he went back there and got with Dizzy and them, and Miles and all of them. When they started all that... Charlie Parker and Dizzy and them got out some new stuff, man, called the Bebop, and I listened to them records -- they had them all around the jukeboxes around here. See, I came home in '43 and stayed down here. I didn't go back up there any more...
